reason: H0 already feeds arbitrary byte buffers and lengths directly to the binary-plist parser through plist_from_bin. Crafted binary plists can select real and Unicode nodes at arbitrary byte offsets, exercising the changed get_unaligned reads in parse_real_node and parse_unicode_node. The supplied change does not expose a distinct entry point, protocol phase, state, configuration, or input domain absent from H0.
evidence: H0 invokes plist_from_bin(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data), size, &root_node) for every fuzz input.
parse_real_node reads fuzz-controlled binary-plist node bytes as uint32_t or uint64_t using get_unaligned.
parse_unicode_node reads fuzz-controlled UTF-16 code units using get_unaligned at *bnode+(i<<1).
Both changed functions are internal binary-plist parsing paths reached through the public entry point used by H0.
recommended_action: Retain H0; no additional fuzz target is materially indicated by this source change.
